statement: For every finite simple undirected graph G, there exists one fixed deterministic algorithm enumerating all nonempty potential maximal cliques of G exactly once, with one fixed polynomial in |V(G)|+|E(G)|+1 bounding time to the first output, every inter-output interval, and time from the final output to termination. The empty vertex graph terminates within that polynomial without output. No graph-class or output-size restriction is imposed; exponential storage is permitted. The complete algorithm and proposed proof are in research/streaming_proof.md.
contribution: Proposed full resolution of the immutable all-PMC polynomial-delay question. The new step is a streaming conversion of the known recursive seed-and-neighborhood enumeration: polynomial-time separator helpers with polynomial fibers pay for seed production, injective lifts transfer child output ranks, and a simultaneous emission-rank/termination induction has an additive polynomial recurrence. Recognition, structural preimages, minimal triangulation, separator extension and buffering are credited prior tools. No fresh correctness, novelty, significance or STOC verdict is claimed.
